statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold after an orderly month-end cash close, while Stress stays elevated on Brent near 90 dollars, a 4.758 percent 10-year yield and hawkish September rate repricing.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a contained, two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning: the Nasdaq-100 traversed its full session range in both directions and closed 27 points below the session high without a failed-retracement chain, while VIX settled near its session low. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI final, ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases on 1 September between 13:45 and 15:00 UTC, where conditional Tail peaks in the watch band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this descriptive assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes August at 29,457 near the session high in an orderly month-end close, with Brent above 90 dollars and a 4.76 percent 10-year keeping Stress elevated
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August month-end session at 29,456.97, up 23.54 points or 0.08 percent, after opening at 29,404.29 and traversing a 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions. The close sits 27 points, about 0.09 percent, below the session high, so the final hour produced a firm but orderly drift into the 20:00 UTC cash close rather than a disorderly rebalancing imbalance. That price path remains the central observation for Tail: retracements were deep and repeatedly successful, pullbacks were not unusually shallow, and there was no chain of failed retracements followed by repeated extension. VIX finished at 14.90, up about 3 percent on the day but near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range, so the volatility bid faded into the close. The Nasdaq-100 also outperformed a weaker broad tape, with the S&P 500 down about 0.3 percent and the Dow down about 0.7 percent, and all three indexes still closed August higher, the Nasdaq by roughly 3 percent. Three channels continue to dominate the backdrop. First, the Strait of Hormuz escalation after U.S. strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iranian retaliation against bases in Jordan lifted WTI about 3 percent to roughly 86 dollars, with Brent settling near 90.5 dollars, against a crisis in its sixth month in which transit traffic is far below pre-war levels. Second, that energy impulse continues to feed a hawkish rate repricing: the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.758 percent, up about 4 basis points and its highest intraday level since January 2025, the 30-year is up 5 basis points to 5.26 percent while the 2-year is broadly unchanged near 4.34 percent, and market-implied odds of a September rate hike stand near 62 percent against roughly 40 percent a week ago following Chairman Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks. Bear steepening of this kind widens the distribution of outcomes, which is why Stress stays elevated even as Tail eases. Third, index-level dispersion remains company-driven rather than macro-driven: Amazon fell more than 3 percent after the FTC and more than twenty state attorneys general sued over undisclosed advertising surcharges, Alphabet fell about 2.3 percent, while Nvidia rose about 1 percent on its 3.5 billion dollar convertible investment in MediaTek and Tesla gained on Hong Kong and Macau price cuts. Offsetting single-name moves of this kind raise dispersion and Stress without producing the index-level directional efficiency that Tail measures. With the cash session closed, the near-term structure is mechanical: the CME maintenance halt runs from 21:00 to 22:00 UTC, after which Globex reopens into thin liquidity. The next substantive checkpoint is the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, which carries the clearest mechanism for a repricing leg capable of denying retracement, and it is the only hour of the forecast horizon mapped above the low band.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours run from the late Sunday Globex reopen through the August month-end U.S. cash close. Tail began at 5 in a quiet, orderly regime, rose to 15 by the 00:00 UTC Asian reprice of the Larak Island strikes, eased back to 5 through the European morning, spiked to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse, and then settled between 9 and 13 across the U.S. session. Stress climbed from 31 to a peak of 55 as oil, long-end yields and September rate-hike odds repriced hawkishly. The action mapping stayed EA_ON and green for all 24 hours, because at no point did the assessed price path show the persistent no-retracement structure that raises Tail. Confidence held between 84 and 88 on continuously available live price and cross-asset evidence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the completed month-end cash close through the Globex maintenance halt, the Asian and European sessions, and into the first September U.S. afternoon. Conditional Tail falls to 7 during the 21:00 UTC halt when no price path can form, drifts between 9 and 11 overnight, firms through the European morning to 13 in the 09:00 UTC hour that produced the prior day's Tail peak, and rises to a conditional peak of 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That is the only hour mapped to WATCH and yellow; every other hour remains EA_ON and green. The danger window stays deliberately narrow at 13:45 to 15:00 UTC, covering the S&P Global PMI final, the double release and the immediate yield-reaction leg. Stress peaks at 64 in the same hour and decays afterwards on the assumption of orderly price discovery. Confidence decays from 88 to 61 with distance from the last live observation, which is the expected horizon effect rather than an evidence problem.
